title: Quentin and the Archive
premise: Jonah Vane, a clone of the murdered archivist Quentin Vane, has spent years alone maintaining a deep-space beacon built to specifications no one will explain. When the ship Meridian returns from a century-long voyage with its crew biologically younger than when they left, Jonah learns the beacon is a lighthouse for two cryosleep arks—one holding the powerful, one holding everyone else—and that the original Quentin was killed for discovering which ark was meant to wake. As factions converge on the archive to seize control of the awakening sequence, Jonah must choose between loyalty to the found family of misfits who've adopted the station and the truth Quentin died protecting: that only one ark can be powered, and the choice was rigged long ago. In the end, Jonah burns the beacon's hidden override, forcing both arks into a shared, slower thaw and giving humanity's fractured halves no choice but to wake together.
about_author: E. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent a decade calibrating signals nobody answered before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who maintain things—machines, promises, and each other.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Jonah Vane's POV. On the lonely beacon station Archive-9, Jonah performs his daily rituals: logging signals, tending the transmitter, rereading the original Quentin's sealed files he can't decrypt. A routine maintenance walk reveals fresh scorch marks on an antenna no ship has visited in years. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Signal From Nowhere
chapters.summary: Jonah intercepts a transmission in Quentin's own voice—recorded decades after his death. Spooked, he contacts his only regular contact, supply pilot Odile Ferro, who arrives early and unannounced with news she shouldn't have: something is coming back from deep space. Emotional beat: first crack in isolation.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The ancient colony ship Meridian decelerates into orbit, broadcasting a distress call in a code retired before Jonah was decanted. Odile and Jonah watch its crew disembark—healthy, laughing, unmistakably twenty years younger than their service records. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Meridian crew, led by a charming captain named Ilsa Reyes, claims a navigation error and asks nothing but supplies. But Jonah notices they avoid the station's lower levels—the archive vaults—and that their medical officer scans the beacon like she knows what it is. Emotional beat: hospitality masking suspicion.

chapters.title: What Quentin Built
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. While the crew sleeps, Odile helps Jonah pry open the vault using Odile's smuggler tools. Inside: schematics for two massive cryosleep arks in lunar orbit, one labeled with a corporate sigil, one blank. The beacon isn't a warning system—it's a countdown trigger. Emotional beat: awe and betrayal.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-referencing crew manifests, Jonah discovers the Meridian launched twice—once publicly, once in secret—and the young crew are the originals, de-aged by time-dilation experiments meant to outlive the arks' sleep cycle. Reyes catches him searching. Emotional beat: caught between charm and threat.

chapters.title: Reyes Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Over dinner, Reyes offers Jonah a place aboard if he hands over the beacon's command keys, framing it as rescue: 'You're a copy keeping a dead man's chair warm.' Jonah refuses without knowing why. Emotional beat: dignity asserted against condescension.

chapters.title: Found Family, Improvised
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile calls in debts and gathers her ragtag circle: disgraced xenolinguist Tam Okafor, ex-corporate auditor Priya Sund, and teenage stowaway mechanic Wren. They hole up at Archive-9 as an improvised household. Emotional beat: warmth kindling amid danger.

chapters.title: The Decryption Party
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam cracks Quentin's sealed files using patterns in the beacon's own transmissions. The final file names Quentin's killer—an executive of Halcyon Combine, owners of Ark One—and reveals the awakening sequence can only power one ark. Emotional beat: grief for a father-figure never met.

chapters.title: Two Arks, One Current
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya audits the power math and confirms it: the beacon can wake Ark One (ten thousand elites) or Ark Two (forty million ordinary people), not both. The Meridian crew were sent to ensure Ark One wakes first. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic against human weight.

chapters.title: Wren Finds the Back Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Teenage Wren, crawling through the station's guts, finds a physical bypass Quentin hid—a manual splice that could split the beacon's output, waking both arks slowly over thirty years instead of instantly. It might also fry the station and everyone in it. Emotional beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Halcyon Arrives
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A Halcyon security flotilla drops out of transit, summoned by Reyes. They quarantine the station, arrest Tam, and announce the beacon will be 'nationalized' for Ark One's awakening. Emotional beat: the machinery of power closing in.

chapters.title: Negotiating With the Future
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes privately admits she aged backward watching her children grow older than her, and begs Jonah to accept the deal—Ark One holds the medical tech to fix people like her. Jonah sees her humanity and still says no. Emotional beat: empathy without surrender.

chapters.title: Tam in the Hold
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Interrogated aboard the Halcyon flagship, Tam stalls by lecturing the security chief on information theory while memorizing deck layouts. Wren infiltrates via a coolant duct to spring them. Emotional beat: defiance dressed as pedantry.

chapters.title: The Escape Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The rescue goes sideways; Odile takes a plasma burn covering their retreat, and Priya stays behind voluntarily, posing as a collaborator to feed them intel. The family regroups, diminished and furious. Emotional beat: cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Quentin's Last Recording
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Decrypted fully at last, Quentin's final message addresses Jonah directly: 'If you're watching this, you're me, and you'll want to know if we chose right.' Quentin confesses he hid the splice because he couldn't bear to choose—and was killed for hesitating. Emotional beat: inheritance of doubt.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. From inside Halcyon, Priya warns the fleet has moved the awakening timetable up: Ark One wakes in seventy-two hours, permanently locking out Ark Two. The team must splice the beacon during the ignition window or lose forty million sleepers. Emotional beat: clock ticking in the blood.

chapters.title: Storming the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The team splits: Odile and Tam draw the flotilla with a decoy broadcast, Wren runs the physical splice, Jonah fights through to the beacon core where Reyes waits, orders in hand but finger hovering off the trigger. Emotional beat: every plan fraying at once.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the core, Jonah offers Reyes the choice Quentin couldn't make—she refuses to be the one who dooms either ark, mirroring his paralysis. Jonah realizes the answer isn't choosing: he triggers the splice himself, burning his hands, splitting the current. Emotional beat: decision as self-acceptance.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Dawn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Both arks begin slow thaws; Halcyon, facing mutiny among crews with families on Ark Two, stands down rather than destroy the beacon and kill their own shareholders' futures. Reyes surrenders her command to testify. Emotional beat: exhausted, improbable victory.

chapters.title: The Long Thaw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Months later, the found family keeps the station running together—Wren apprenticed to the beacon, Tam cataloguing Quentin's archive, Odile flying again. First sleepers from both arks wake to strangers waiting with coffee and questions. Emotional beat: tenderness after siege.

chapters.title: Quentin and the Archive
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah adds his own entry to the archive beside Quentin's, addressed to whoever maintains this next: 'We didn't choose. We refused to.' Watching the first joint shuttle rise between the arks, he finally feels like an original. Emotional beat: peace earned, legacy claimed.
